root_cause.runtime_water: The physical-corridor maps hid their authored capture ribbons during play, while ARaftSimWaterSurfaceActor forced ActiveLiveSurfaceCoverage to zero under the obsolete assumption that authored water remained visible below it.
root_cause.vegetation: The physical-corridor fallback placed up to 12000 converted ProceduralVegetationEditor alpha-card trees, dominated by one broadleaf form, producing repeated cutout walls and sparse ground cover.

implemented_contract.saved_map_water_authority: ARaftSimRiverWaterConfig explicitly records solver-owned runtime rendering and river-specific coverage, color, roughness, specular, and wet-bank feather values.
implemented_contract.backward_compatibility: Older physical maps with hidden actors tagged RaftSimLiveSolverWaterOwnsRuntimeRendering promote the live mesh through a fail-closed tag migration instead of rendering no river.
implemented_contract.vegetation_material: opaque one-sided DefaultLit vertex-color material; no alpha cards
implemented_contract.placement: 6200 deterministic source-mask and slope-screened HISM instances per river; 4650 canopy and 1550 shrub/ground-cover instances
implemented_contract.authority: procedural visual infill only; no terrain, collision, wet/dry, solver, bathymetry, species, or guide authority

assertions_added: exactly one live solver surface actor
visible carrier follows saved or migrated ownership
calm and active coverage are nonzero and ordered

accepted: The gameplay river is visible across the calm launch instead of exposing black or brown terrain as water.
The moving solver mesh no longer depends on a hidden authored ribbon.
The sampled wet bank uses a narrow feather rather than a broad rectangular land overlay.
Opaque volumetric forms remove the former alpha-card cutout wall and add explicit shrubs and ground cover.
rejected: The procedural lobes remain stylized, too repetitive, and insufficiently species-specific for photoreal approval.
Near-bank terrain remains broad and dark and needs source-scale rock, sediment, litter, moss, grass, and shoreline breakup.
Calm water remains too uniform and bright toward the horizon; production water needs richer depth, reflection, transmission, and hydraulic structure.
Neither frame demonstrates a surveyed rapid, accepted guide line, production spray/aeration, or target-hardware performance.

required_external_acceptance_gates: qualified local-guide review of rapid stationing, runnable lines, hazards, flow bands, scouting, recovery, and portage behavior
geospatial review of route registration, vertical datum, terrain, bank breaklines, rock geometry, and bathymetry
hydraulic calibration and convergence approval against observed rapid behavior
ecology and geology approval of species, density, ground cover, wet banks, boulders, and seasonal context
named environment-art and water-VFX approval for lifelike terrain, foliage, water, foam, spray, mist, shoreline contact, and raft occlusion
rights and publication approval for all source imagery, cultural/place-name context, and public hazard/access information
packaged desktop, console-quality, handheld, and VR performance plus collision, capsize, recovery, and full-run gameplay acceptance
